The team played in [[Major League Soccer]] (MLS), the top flight of club soccer in the United States, as a member of the [[Eastern Conference (MLS)|Eastern Conference]]. The year also marked the 22nd season of first-division club soccer in [[South Florida]]. In addition to playing in the [[2025 Major League Soccer season|MLS regular season]], Inter Miami CF competed in the [[2025 CONCACAF Champions Cup|CONCACAF Champions Cup]] for the second time, and played in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] for the first time.{{cite news |last=Deen |first=Safid |date=November 12, 2024 |title=Messi breaks silence on Inter Miami's playoff exit. What's next for his time in the US? |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2024/11/12/messi-inter-miami-playoff-exit-whats-next-mls-argentina/76200848007/ |work=[[USA Today]] |accessdate=November 13, 2024}} The club were the defending [[Supporters' Shield]] champions, having set a record for most [[points (association football)|points]] in MLS history during the [[2024 Inter Miami CF season|2024 regular season]]. They qualified for the FIFA Club World Cup in the allocated slot for the host country and hosted the expanded tournament's opening match on June 15, 2025, at [[Hard Rock Stadium]] in [[Miami Gardens, Florida]].{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |author-link=Michelle Kaufman |date=October 20, 2024 |title=Inter Miami earns spot in 2025 Club World Cup, will play opener at Hard Rock Stadium |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article294243004.html |work=[[Miami Herald]] |url-access=limited |accessdate=November 13, 2024}} The 2025 season was the final year for the club at [[Chase Stadium]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida|Fort Lauderdale]], which was replaced by [[Nu Stadium]] in 2026.{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=September 4, 2024 |title='We're Coming Home:' Inter Miami kicks off countdown to opening of Miami Freedom Park |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article291872690.html |work=Miami Herald |url-access=limited |accessdate=November 19, 2024}} Inter Miami CF ended the season with their first [[MLS Cup]] title after they defeated [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC]] 3–1 in the [[MLS Cup 2025|final]] played at Chase Stadium.{{cite news |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=December 6, 2025 |title=Messi and Inter Miami have completed their journey. They win the MLS Cup, topping Vancouver 3-1 |url=https://apnews.com/article/messi-mls-cup-inter-miami-vancouver-4773da0271b60e61ffbe6d697da34245 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=December 13, 2025}} ==Summary== ===Preseason=== Argentinian manager [[Gerardo Martino|Gerardo "Tata" Martino]] resigned at the end of the 2024 season after two years at the club and was replaced on November 26 by [[Javier Mascherano]], the former manager of the [[Argentina national under-20 football team|Argentina under-20 team]].{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=November 22, 2024 |title=Tata Martino bids farewell to Inter Miami, Javier Mascherano expected to be next coach |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article295962169.html |work=Miami Herald |accessdate=November 22, 2024}}{{cite news |last=Cardenas |first=Felipe |date=November 26, 2024 |title=Inter Miami names Javier Mascherano as new head coach |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5948934/2024/11/26/inter-miami-javier-mascherano-confirmed/ |work=[[The Athletic]] |url-access=subscription |accessdate=November 26, 2024}} Sporting director [[Chris Henderson]] left Miami in December to join [[Atlanta United FC]].{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=December 16, 2024 |title=Inter Miami sporting director Chris Henderson leaves for conference rival Atlanta United |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article297152819.html |work=Miami Herald |accessdate=December 16, 2024}} The team's [[captain (association football)|captain]], Argentinian midfielder [[Lionel Messi]], has a contract through the end of the 2025 season.{{cite news |last=Cardenas |first=Felipe |date=November 10, 2024 |title=Inter Miami, Messi and Martino are out: What went wrong and what comes next? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5911359/2024/11/10/inter-miami-messi-future-mls-playoffs/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |accessdate=November 13, 2024}} The team had several key players who had contracts that were set to expire during the 2024–25 offseason, including striker [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] and defender [[Jordi Alba]], who had a club option for 2025.{{cite magazine |last=Chalker |first=Braden |date=November 12, 2024 |title=Which Players Should Inter Miami Re-sign for 2025 season? |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/which-players-should-inter-miami-re-sign-for-2025-season |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=November 13, 2024}} Suárez signed a one-year extension of his contract on November 27 and was followed by the exercising of a contract option for Alba through the 2025 season.{{cite news |last=Becherano |first=Lizzy|date=November 27, 2024 |title=Luis Suárez signs new Inter Miami contract through to 2025 |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/42642886/luis-suarez-signs-new-inter-miami-contract-2025 |publisher=ESPN |accessdate=March 14, 2025}}{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=December 9, 2024 |title=Alba to return to Inter Miami for 2025. Freire is gone. Who else is staying? Going? |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article296801294.html |work=Miami Herald |accessdate=March 14, 2025}} The preseason for Inter Miami CF began on January 10 with players reporting to a training camp that expended to full sessions three days later.{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=January 13, 2025 |title=Messi, Inter Miami open training camp under new coach Mascherano. Here's how it went |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article298441663.html |work=Miami Herald |accessdate=January 21, 2025}} The team played their first friendly match ten days later against [[Club América]] of [[Liga MX]] at [[Allegiant Stadium]] in the [[Las Vegas]] area. The teams drew 2–2 in regulation time and Inter Miami CF won 3–2 in the [[penalty shootout (association football)|penalty shootout]], which culminated in a winning kick by 17-year-old homegrown player [[Santiago Morales (soccer)|Santiago Morales]].{{cite news |last=Butler |first=Dylan |date=January 18, 2025 |title=Lionel Messi scores in Inter Miami preseason win over Club América |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/lionel-messi-scores-in-inter-miami-cf-preseason-win-over-club-america |work=MLSsoccer.com |accessdate=January 21, 2025}} Inter Miami CF then played in three overseas friendlies organized by marketing agency Never Say Never (co-founded by [[Andrés Iniesta]]) before returning to the United States in February.{{cite news |last=Anzidei |first=Melanie |date=January 10, 2025 |title=Lionel Messi and Inter Miami expand preseason tour to five games across the Americas |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6053340/2025/01/10/inter-miami-messi-tour/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |accessdate=January 21, 2025}} Inter Miami CF and [[Orlando City SC]] played a preseason [[friendly match]] on February 14 at [[Raymond James Stadium]]; it was the first match at the stadium with MLS teams since the [[Tampa Bay Mutiny]] folded in 2001.{{cite news |last=Encina |first=Eduardo A. |date=November 4, 2024 |title=Lionel Messi, Inter Miami to play preseason match in Tampa |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/2024/11/04/lionel-messi-inter-miami-raymond-james-stadium-mls-/ |work=[[Tampa Bay Times]] |accessdate=November 17, 2024}} ===February and March=== Miami began their season with the first round of the [[2025 CONCACAF Champions Cup|CONCACAF Champions Cup]]. The first leg was hosted by [[Sporting Kansas City]] and originally scheduled for February 18, but was moved a day later due to a winter storm warning. The match kicked off on February 19 with a temperature of {{convert|5|F|C}}; by the end of the match, the temperature was below {{convert|0|F|C}}.{{cite news |last=Becherano |first=Lizzy |date=February 19, 2025 |title=Frigid conditions in Inter Miami CCC win 'not human' - Mascherano |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/43928865/frigid-conditions-inter-miami-ccc-win-not-human-mascherano |publisher=ESPN |accessdate=February 20, 2025}}{{cite news |last=Abnos |first=Alexander |date=February 20, 2025 |title=Could Messi do it on an inhumanely cold night in Kansas City? Of course he could |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/feb/20/lionel-messi-inter-miami-cold |work=The Guardian |accessdate=February 20, 2025}} Lionel Messi scored the lone goal of the match in the 56th minute as both teams had difficulty playing in the cold conditions.{{cite news |last=Cardenas |first=Felipe |date=February 19, 2025 |title=Lionel Messi, Inter Miami tame the Kansas City cold in Concacaf Champions Cup |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6147971/2025/02/19/messi-inter-miami-sporting-kansas-city-concacaf-champions-cup/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |accessdate=February 20, 2025}} The match's referee, Marco Ortíz of Mexico, was later suspended by [[CONCACAF]] for requesting an autograph from Messi for a family member.{{cite news |last=Becherano |first=Lizzy |date=February 20, 2025 |title=Concacaf disciplines ref for Lionel Messi autograph request |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/43945095/concacaf-disciplines-ref-lionel-messi-autograph-request |publisher=ESPN |accessdate=February 23, 2025}} The team returned to Florida three days later to open the MLS regular season against [[New York City FC]]; the scheduled kickoff time was delayed by five hours to accommodate the earlier change in the CONCACAF Champions Cup fixture.{{cite press release |date=February 18, 2025 |title=Saturday's MLS Match Time Change: Inter Miami CF vs. NYCFC Now Set for 7:30 p.m. ET |url=https://www.intermiamicf.com/news/saturday-s-mls-match-time-change-inter-miami-cf-vs-nycfc-now-set-for-7-30-p-m-et |publisher=Inter Miami CF |accessdate=February 23, 2025}} Messi had two assists in the match, which finished in a 2–2 draw after a late tying goal for Miami in the tenth minute of stoppage time by [[Telasco Segovia]]. Miami had played for most of the match with 10 players after defender [[Tomás Avilés]] was sent off for a tackle in the 23rd minute.{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=February 23, 2025 |title=Messi's two assists help Inter Miami salvage 2-2 tie vs. NYCFC in dramatic MLS opener |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article300666064.html |work=Miami Herald |url-access=subscription |accessdate=February 23, 2025}} Miami advanced to the round of 16 in the Champions Cup with a 3–1 win at home against Sporting Kansas City in the second leg of their series, which finished with a 4–1 [[aggregate score]]. All three goals for the home team were scored in the first half, including two in stoppage time.{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=February 25, 2025 |title=Inter Miami beats KC 3-1, advances in Champions Cup with goals by Messi, Allende, Suarez |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/mls/inter-miami/article300867074.html |work=Miami Herald |accessdate=March 2, 2025}} Lionel Messi did not travel for Miami's away league match against the [[Houston Dynamo]], who allowed fans in attendance to claim a complimentary ticket for a future match. Miami won 4–1 with a goal and three assists from [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]].{{cite news |last=Warren |first=Sam |date=March 2, 2025 |title=Houston Dynamo fall to Inter Miami CF on a disappointing night without Lionel Messi |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/dynamo/article/dynamo-vs-inter-miami-match-recap-20192092.php |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |accessdate=March 2, 2025}} ==Non-competitive== ===Preseason=== The full preseason schedule with matches in Central and South America was announced on January 10, 2025.{{cite press release |date=January 10, 2025 |title=The Americas Preseason Tour: Inter Miami CF Unveils 2025 Preseason |url=https://www.intermiamicf.com/news/the-americas-preseason-tour-inter-miami-cf-unveils-2025-preseason |publisher=Inter Miami CF |access-date=January 10, 2025}} {{football box collapsible | round = 1 | date = January 18 | time = 10:00 pm [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]] | team1 = Inter Miami CF {{fbaicon|USA}} | score = 2–2 | report = https://www.intermiamicf.com/competitions/friendly/2025/matches/miavsame-01-18-2025/ | team2 = {{fbaicon|MEX}} [[Club América|América]] | goals1 = *[[Lionel Messi|Messi]] {{goal|34}} *[[Yannick Bright|Bright]] {{yel|73}} *[[Tomás Avilés|Avilés]] {{goal|90+2}} | goals2 = *[[Henry Martín|Martín]] {{goal|31}} *[[Ramón Juárez|Juárez]] {{yel|47}} *[[Israel Reyes|Reyes]] {{goal|52}} | penaltyscore = 3–2 | penalties1 = *[[Federico Redondo|Redondo]] {{penmiss}} *[[David Martínez (footballer, born 1998)|Martínez]] {{pengoal}} *[[Julian Gressel|Gressel]] {{penmiss}} *[[David Ruiz (footballer, born 2004)|Ruiz]] {{pengoal}} *[[Marcelo Weigandt|Weigandt]] {{penmiss}} *[[Santiago Morales (soccer)|Morales]] {{pengoal}} | penalties2 = *{{penmiss}} [[Víctor Dávila|Dávila]] *{{penmiss}} [[Alan Cervantes|Cervantes]] *{{penmiss}} [[Richard Sánchez (Paraguayan footballer)|R.
